cards.name: Push (Legacy)
cards.summary: Clip B slides in from one edge and shoves clip A out of the opposite edge, both frames moving together at constant speed with no blur. Default direction (seen in the gallery render): B enters from the left and A exits right. This is the pre-2026 Push kept for old projects; the new Film Impact 'Push' replaces it.
use_for: move between two locations or speakers in an explainer
step to the next item in a listicle or news-roundup reel
carousel-style card change in a social reel
chronology beats (left-to-right reads as forward in time)
avoid: at 1 s or longer it looks like a 2000s slideshow; keep it short
no motion blur, so a fast push strobes; use the new 'Push' instead
do not mix push directions at random within one piece
cards.equivalent: PR replacement: 'Push' (new GPU transition with easing and motion blur; exact name 'Push', a separate list entry). AE: keyframe Position of both layers by one frame width (A from 0 to +W, B from -W to 0 for the default left-to-right) with Easy Ease and motion blur on.
cards.scripting: Applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 130 s cut (landed 129.52-130.52 s); the gallery render shows a clean left-to-right push. Centred needs about 0.5 s of handles on both clips. Single-sided on an upper track it pushes in over the clip below; on V1 it pushes against black. Direction is a transition setting in Effect Controls, not a spec prop; the default (West to East) is what you get.

verified.note: B enters from the left and A is pushed out right, both images moving together with a hard vertical seam and no blur (half and half at the cut).

cards.name: Random Blocks
cards.summary: Clip B appears in small rectangular blocks that pop in at random positions until they cover clip A.
use_for: 'data loading' or digitisation reveal in a tech or AI explainer
deliberately retro joke beat in a satire reel
reveal a document or screenshot as if it is being decoded
hack or leak story beat paired with a glitch SFX
avoid: reads as a cheap 90s video toaster in serious documentary or news
over about 1 s it drags
hard block edges alias on detailed footage
cards.equivalent: AE: Block Dissolve on the outgoing layer, keyframe Transition Completion 0 to 100% (set Block Width/Height, Feather 0, Soft Edges off), or CC Grid Wipe for a more ordered version.
cards.scripting: Block size (width/height count) is a Custom setting in Effect Controls, not a spec prop; the default gives small rectangles (gallery render confirms B popping in as random blocks). Applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 134 s cut (133.52-134.52 s); centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: Rectangular blocks of B pop in at random positions over A, about half covered at the cut and nearly all B by 0.3 s after.

cards.name: Random Invert
cards.summary: Random blocks of clip A flip to a colour negative until the whole frame is inverted, then clip B replaces the negative block by block. An old Dissolve-folder transition kept for old projects.
use_for: one-off 'shock' or 'system error' beat in a satire reel
negative or x-ray flash into a reveal
glitch accent on a hacking or leak story
avoid: inverted faces look ugly; never on a leader's close-up
strobing negatives can bother photosensitive viewers; keep it short and rare
looks dated in serious news or documentary
cards.equivalent: PR replacement: 'Glitch' or 'Solarize' (new GPU transitions). AE: on the outgoing layer add Invert, then Block Dissolve animated 0 to 100% with the incoming clip below; or a 2-3 frame Invert flash on hold keyframes at the cut.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015 but still applies by name: harvest placed it with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 138 s cut (137.52-138.52 s); the gallery render shows A going negative in blocks, then B arriving in blocks. Invert source/destination and block size are Custom settings, not spec props. Single-sided it would only invert one clip against black, so use it centred.

verified.note: Random blocks of A turn negative, the whole frame is a colour negative at the cut, then B shows through with leftover negative blocks.

cards.name: Random Wipe
cards.summary: Clip B is revealed by small blocks that fill in at random along a moving front, giving a ragged pixel wipe. Default direction (gallery render): top to bottom.
use_for: retro 'download' style reveal of a graphic or chart
playful alternative to a straight wipe in an AI-education reel
transition into a low-res screen recording or archival clip
map or data panel reveal in an explainer
avoid: looks like a 2000s DVD menu in serious documentary
hard block edges shimmer on fine detail at small sizes
cards.equivalent: AE: Gradient Wipe on the outgoing layer using a gradient layer built from a Ramp combined with blocky noise (Fractal Noise then Mosaic), keyframe Transition Completion; or Block Dissolve and Linear Wipe together.
cards.scripting: Direction is set in Effect Controls, not a spec prop; the default sweeps top to bottom. Applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 142 s cut (141.52-142.52 s); centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: B fills in from the top with a ragged block-stepped front, covering the top half at the cut and all but a bottom strip after.

cards.name: Roll Away
cards.summary: Clip A rolls up like a scroll from its left edge toward the right: the rolled part is a narrow squashed strip that travels across and off the right edge, uncovering clip B behind it.
use_for: mock 'old newspaper or scroll' gag in a satire reel
deliberately kitsch retro beat
turning past an old document page in an archival segment
avoid: reads as a cheap 2000s wedding DVD in any serious edit
the rolled strip is just a squashed slice of clip A with no real 3D shading, so it looks flat and soft
cards.equivalent: PR replacement: 'Page Peel' (new GPU transition). AE: CC Page Turn on the outgoing layer with a large Fold Radius and Fold Position animated across the frame.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; still applies by name: harvest placed it with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 146 s cut (145.52-146.52 s); gallery render shows the left-to-right roll. Centred needs handles on both clips. Roll direction is a Custom setting, not a spec prop.

verified.note: A narrow squashed strip of A travels left to right across the frame, uncovering B on its left while the rest of A stays flat on its right.

cards.name: Slash Slide
cards.summary: Diagonal strips of clip B fly in at staggered speeds and slide over clip A until they join into the full frame.
use_for: energetic rally or sports montage beat when kept very short
retro TV-promo parody in a satire reel
opening a 'versus' comparison
avoid: at normal speed it looks like a cheap 2000s TV promo
strip edges are hard and aliased
cards.equivalent: PR replacement: 'Slice' (new GPU transition, cleaner diagonal cut). AE: CC Line Sweep or Venetian Blinds at about 45 degrees on the outgoing layer, or several masked diagonal strips of the incoming layer with staggered Position keyframes.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 150 s cut (149.52-150.52 s); gallery render shows diagonal strips of B cascading in over A. Strip count and direction are Custom settings, not spec props.

verified.note: Staggered diagonal strips of B slide over A, few at first, interleaved at the cut, nearly joined by 0.3 s after.

cards.name: Slide (Legacy)
cards.summary: Clip B slides in from an edge and covers clip A, which stays still underneath. Default direction (gallery render): B enters from the left. This is the pre-2026 Slide kept for old projects.
use_for: bring a full-frame card or graphic in over footage
next-item step in a listicle reel
single-sided on an upper track: slide a document or tweet screenshot in over B-roll
avoid: constant speed with no blur looks like PowerPoint; keep it short or use eased keyframes
wrong tone for emotional documentary moments
cards.equivalent: PR: no new GPU transition named 'Slide' appears in the 2026 list; use the new 'Push', or animate Position on a Transform effect with easing for a modern slide. AE: keyframe Position of the incoming layer from off-frame to centre with Easy Ease and motion blur.
cards.scripting: Applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 154 s cut (153.52-154.52 s); centred needs handles on both clips. Direction (8 options) is set in Effect Controls, not a spec prop; the default (from the left) is used.

verified.note: B (shifted, so it is moving) slides in from the left over A, which stays still underneath; hard vertical edge, half-way at the cut.

cards.name: Sliding Bands
cards.summary: Thin vertical bands of clip B open up in clip A and widen until they join into the full frame, like vertical blinds opening. The opening is staggered from left to right: the left side is already solid B while the bands on the right are still thin.
use_for: retro TV-graphics parody
reveal a striped or text-heavy graphic
quick move into a split-screen or comparison
avoid: looks dated outside a parody
busy bands fight with on-screen text
cards.equivalent: PR: closest new GPU transitions are 'Stripe' (flat bands) or 'Louver' (3D slats). AE: Venetian Blinds on the outgoing layer (Direction 90 degrees for vertical bands) animating Transition Completion 0 to 100%.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 158 s cut (157.52-158.52 s). Gallery render shows the default: many thin vertical bands of B widening. Band count/direction are Custom settings, not spec props.

verified.note: Thin vertical bands of B open and widen into A, but staggered left to right: only the left third has bands at -0.3 s and only thin A slats remain on the right at +0.3 s.

cards.name: Sliding Boxes
cards.summary: Vertical bars made of clip B slide across the screen one after another until clip B fills the frame.
use_for: retro game-show or TV-promo parody
reveal a bar-chart style graphic
fast step between two list items
avoid: dated and busy in serious news or documentary
bars cut through faces and on-screen text
cards.equivalent: PR replacement: 'Louver' or 'Slice' (new GPU transitions). AE: masked vertical strips of the incoming layer with staggered Position keyframes (Sequence Layers or offset keys), or Card Wipe with 1 row and several columns.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 162 s cut (161.52-162.52 s); gallery render shows vertical bars of B interleaving with A. Bar count is a Custom setting, not a spec prop.

verified.note: Vertical bars of B about one-eighth frame wide enter in sequence, alternating with A bars at the cut, until B covers the frame.

cards.name: Spin
cards.summary: Clip B grows from a thin vertical strip in the centre to full width over clip A, like a card turning on a vertical axis but drawn flat (a horizontal scale, no perspective). Clip A stays still behind.
use_for: 'flip side' or 'other side of the story' gag in a satire reel
flip between a claim and a fact-check card
playful product or tool reveal in an AI-education reel
avoid: no perspective or motion blur, so it reads as cheap 2000s
a long spin feels slow; keep it under a second
cards.equivalent: PR: the closest new GPU transition is 'Flip Motion' (real 3D flip with perspective and motion blur). Not '3D Spin' or 'Spin Motion': those twirl the image in the frame plane. AE: on the incoming layer keyframe Scale X 0 to 100% with the anchor at the centre (exact match), or make it 3D and keyframe Y Rotation 90 to 0 degrees with Easy Ease and motion blur for a nicer version.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 166 s cut (165.52-166.52 s); gallery render shows B opening out from a centre strip. Centred needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: B grows from a narrow centred strip to nearly full width over still A, horizontally squeezed with no perspective.

cards.name: Spin Away
cards.summary: Like Spin, clip B turns into view from a thin strip in the centre on a vertical axis, but drawn with perspective: the panel is a trapezoid (one edge taller than the other) while it turns, then lands full frame over clip A.
use_for: satirical 'twist' beat in a political reel
turn from one leader's quote card to another's
retro comedy transition
avoid: looks like a 2000s wedding DVD in serious edits
perspective distortion is ugly on faces and text mid-spin
cards.equivalent: PR: the closest new GPU transition is 'Flip Motion' (3D flip with motion blur); '3D Spin' twirls into depth instead. AE: 3D incoming layer with Y Rotation keyframed 90 to 0 degrees, anchor at centre, a camera for perspective, motion blur on.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 170 s cut (169.52-170.52 s). Gallery render: same centre-strip opening as Spin but with a perspective-skewed panel; that skew is the only visible difference.

verified.note: B opens from a centred strip as a trapezoid panel (left edge shorter than right) over A and widens toward full frame.

cards.name: Spiral Boxes
cards.summary: A band of boxes travels round the frame edge and spirals in toward the centre, replacing clip A with clip B box by box.
use_for: retro game-show or quiz parody in a satire reel
'closing in' reveal of a central subject
kids-style AI-education explainer beat
avoid: too slow and busy for news or documentary
the last boxes land on the centre, often right on a face
cards.equivalent: AE: no single effect; Gradient Wipe with a hand-built spiral-order gradient layer (grid of grey squares stepping in value), or CC Grid Wipe for a simpler grid reveal.
cards.scripting: Box counts (horizontal/vertical) are Custom settings in Effect Controls, not spec props; defaults are used. Applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 174 s cut (173.52-174.52 s); gallery render shows B filling in round the edges and closing on the centre, and it reads at 1 s.

verified.note: B fills in around the frame edge (top, right, then bottom) leaving a shrinking central rectangle of A, a small strip by 0.3 s after.

cards.name: Stretch
cards.summary: Clip B starts squeezed thin against the left edge and stretches across the frame, covering clip A, which stays put. This is the old Stretch-folder version, not the new GPU 'Stretch'.
use_for: comic 'stretching the truth' gag in a satire reel
retro cartoon-style transition
stretch a graphic card into frame
avoid: distorts faces and text during the move
looks dated next to modern motion-blurred transitions
cards.equivalent: PR: the new GPU 'Stretch' has the same name and cannot be reached by name (see scripting); 'Stretch Wipe' is the scriptable modern alternative. AE: keyframe Scale X of the incoming layer 0 to 100% with the anchor point on its left edge, or CC Scale Wipe.
cards.scripting: Name clash: Premiere 2026 lists two transitions named 'Stretch' (list index 44 = this old one, index 144 = the new GPU one). getVideoTransitionByName('Stretch') returns THIS old one: the gallery renders for index 44 and 144 are the same frames (pixel diff only compression noise). So a spec asking for 'Stretch' always gets this squeeze-from-the-left look. Harvest placed it with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 178 s cut (177.52-178.52 s).

verified.note: B, squeezed thin against the left edge, stretches rightward over a static A (about half width at the cut).

cards.name: Stretch In
cards.summary: Clip B appears over clip A stretched very wide, then un-stretches to its normal shape while fading in.
use_for: 'snap into focus' reveal of a quote card
comic emphasis entry in a meme reel
retro cartoon-style transition
avoid: stretched faces look grotesque mid-move
dated outside a deliberate retro or comic tone
cards.equivalent: PR: no modern by-name match (the new GPU 'Stretch' shares its name with the old one and is unreachable by name); 'Stretch Wipe' is the nearest scriptable modern elastic transition. AE: on the incoming layer keyframe Scale X from about 300% to 100% together with Opacity 0 to 100%, Easy Ease out.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 182 s cut (181.52-182.52 s). Gallery render confirms B fading in hugely stretched sideways (streaky) and settling to normal.

verified.note: B fades in hugely stretched horizontally (smeared streaks at the cut) and is still somewhat wide 0.3 s after as it settles.

cards.name: Stretch Over
cards.summary: Clip B appears as a thin full-width horizontal band across the middle, squashed vertically, and stretches up and down over clip A until it fills the frame.
use_for: 'opening up' reveal of a big statement card
comic stretch beat in a meme or satire reel
retro TV-promo parody
avoid: distorts faces and text while it moves
dated in serious news or documentary
cards.equivalent: PR: no modern by-name match ('Stretch Wipe' is the nearest scriptable elastic transition). AE: on the incoming layer keyframe Scale Y 0 to 100% with the anchor point at the centre (Scale X stays 100%).
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 186 s cut (185.52-186.52 s). Gallery render shows the centre band opening vertically.

verified.note: B is a vertically squashed full-width band across the middle that grows taller (70 px, 170 px, 290 px of 360) over A.

cards.name: Swap
cards.summary: Clips A and B trade places like shuffled cards: A slides out to one side and behind while B slides out the other way and comes to the front.
use_for: 'this vs that' or before-and-after comparison beat
flip between two leaders' statements in a satire reel
shuffle through photos in a listicle reel
avoid: looks like a 2000s slideshow template if held long
needs two full clips; meaningless against black
at the midpoint the two images part by a thin gap that shows whatever is underneath (the gallery render showed a garbage-coloured strip); keep a solid or footage layer on the track below
cards.equivalent: AE: two layers with Position keyframes moving out to opposite sides and back, swapping stacking order at the midpoint (or 3D layers with Z Position pushed back on A), motion blur on.
cards.scripting: Believed hidden from the Effects panel since CC 2015; applied by name with no error, 1.0 s centred on the 190 s cut (189.52-190.52 s); gallery render shows A sliding aside while B comes out from behind and takes the front. Use centred only; needs handles on both clips.

verified.note: A slides left and B slides right from behind it, side by side at the cut, then both slide back with B in front; a thin gap between them showed a teal/pink garbage strip at the cut.
